text:
IncidentBot: [ALERT] 03:00 UTC - high tail latency for /v1/generate (p99 > 2s) — paging oncall
Maya: saw this alert, looks like a burst from a small customer group hitting long contexts. p95 also up but p50 normal.
Maya: @leon you oncall? can you confirm and take point if needed
Leon: I’m awake, taking it. joining debug. first pass: checking node distribution and recent deploys.
Leon: @DeployBot show deploys --since 2h
DeployBot: recent deploys: model-routing v1.4.2 @ 02:10 UTC (canary->stable), infra patch on gateway 01:40 UTC
Ben: adding context — we ran a rebalancer job at 01:55 to migrate KV shards, might overlap with the canary.
Sara: customer-impact estimate? are requests 5xx or just slow?
Leon: mostly 200s but long tail latency. graph: 
```
query: rails.serve_latency.p99{route:/v1/generate} by (region)
result: us-west 2.1s, eu-west 1.8s, apac 0.9s
```
Leon: looks like us-west cluster taking brunt. connections and queue depth on a subset of workers spiked.
Maya: probable cause: rebalancer + canary created hotspot on a small set of GPUs.
Maya: mitigation plan: 1) route traffic away from affected workers 2) temporary autoscale bump for us-west ded pool 3) add short maintenance window for rebalancer to finish without alert storm
Ben: I can route steady-state traffic to fallback model-compact variant for affected tenant IDs. that should reduce per-token time.
Leon: doing routing change now: 
```bash
# switch policy for tenant group alpha to fallback route
redwoodctl route update --tenant alpha --policy fallback-compact --dry-run && redwoodctl route update --tenant alpha --policy fallback-compact
```
Leon: applied. monitoring...
Maya: flipping alert severity to P2 for this thread to reduce noise while we stabilize. noted in pager. :white_check_mark:
IncidentBot: Pager update: severity set to P2 by Maya at 03:12 UTC
Leon: initiating autoscale bump: redwoodctl pool scale --pool us-west-dedicated --replicas +3
DeployBot: autoscale request accepted, new replicas starting (3)
Sara: starting to see p99 drop in us-west from 2.1s -> 1.4s within 7m. customer error rates still low.
Ben: routing change helped; compact model has slightly lower quality but we’re in mitigation. will notify support for potential customer comms if degraded quality persists.
Maya: key decisions so far: routing fallback applied, autoscale bump, severity lowered. next: post-incident tuning — we should avoid recurring noise from the rebalancer + canary interaction.
Maya: suggested follow-ups: 
- add short-term suppression on alert rule that fires on transient node-rebalance events (not on sustained latency)
- create a dashboard tile that correlates rebalancer job runs + per-worker queue depth + p99 latency
- validate threshold logic: current alert fires on p99 > 1.5s for any region for 1m — maybe change to 3m or add worker_count filter
Leon: +1. I can prototype a Grafana panel and add a rule that requires sustained elevation for 3m and >10% of workers affected before paging.
Ben: also recommend tracking source by tenant and model-variant so we can auto-fallback in future without human routing. create a label in the alert query.
Sara: can someone own cleaning up the noise after the incident (silence/schedule)? we should prefer scheduled maintenance windows vs one-off silences.
Maya: I’ll open a post-incident task: "monitoring: rebalancer interaction - tune alert window + dashboard" and assign to Leon + Ben. includes: tuning rule, dashboard, test plan.
Maya: setting a temporary maintenance window for the rebalancer job tonight 00:00-02:00 UTC to avoid cascading alerts while we roll a durable fix. (Ops runbook step)
Leon: created dashboard panel draft: link: https://grafana.redwood.company/d/abc123/rebalancer-latency (will add node-level drilldowns).
Ben: after we agree on thresholds, I’ll run a synthetic load test to verify no false positives. plan: run 5m ramp to 2x traffic, verify p99 < new-threshold for sustained 3m.
Sara: support notification: notify top-10 affected tenants that we applied fallback route and quality may be slightly lower. Ben, can you draft message?
Ben: drafting now. will post to #customer-updates and ping SEs for any sensitive accounts.
IncidentBot: Alert resolved at 03:38 UTC — p99 back to normal range in all regions.
Maya: marking incident as mitigated. leaving follow-ups:
1) Leon: push alert rule change to staging (require 3m sustained, >=10% workers) — due EOD
2) Ben: implement tenant -> auto-fallback labels and test — due 48h
3) Sara: coordinate customer comms for any tenants that saw degraded quality — due next business day
4) Maya: schedule postmortem + monitoring review meeting for tomorrow 10:00 UTC
Leon: will validate rule in staging and post results here with query + screenshots.
Ben: will run synthetic test in staging and attach logs.
Sara: I'll draft customer notices and get approvals.
Maya: also added a short-term playbook note to runbook: when rebalancer + canary overlap, prefer temporary route fallback before scaling to avoid cross-shard hotspots.
Leon: final note — we should consider adding a probe that detects rebalancer activity and mutes short-lived latency spikes automatically (mute for 10m). adding to backlog.
Maya: thanks everyone. closing incident thread, will update the ticket with links to dashboard + rule PR once done. :v:
